# Web App — Complete Blueprint
## Generated by LASA | February 25, 2026 | Full-Stack Web Application

## Universal Design & Code Quality Standards

These rules apply to EVERY component, page, and section in this project. Violating any of these is a build failure. The AI coding tool that receives this blueprint MUST follow all of them.

### Spacing & Layout

- Use a consistent spacing scale based on 4px increments: 4px (0.25rem), 8px (0.5rem), 12px (0.75rem), 16px (1rem), 24px (1.5rem), 32px (2rem), 48px (3rem), 64px (4rem), 96px (6rem).
- Section vertical padding: `py-16 sm:py-20 lg:py-24` minimum. Never less than `py-12` on any section.
- Container: `max-w-7xl mx-auto px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8`. Every section's content must be constrained — nothing runs edge-to-edge unless explicitly specified.
- Card internal padding: `p-6 sm:p-8` minimum. Content inside cards must breathe.
- Grid gap: `gap-4 sm:gap-6 lg:gap-8` between items. Never `gap-1` or `gap-2` for primary layout grids.
- Heading margin-bottom: `mb-4` to `mb-6`. Never place a heading directly against body text with zero spacing.
- Body text line-height: `leading-relaxed` (1.625) minimum. Dense text walls are unreadable.
- No margin-top on the first child or margin-bottom on the last child of any container.
- Vertical rhythm: maintain consistent spacing between all repeating elements (cards, list items, sections).

### Typography

- Heading hierarchy must be visually obvious: each level (h1 → h2 → h3 → h4) must have a clear size step. Never use the same size for two heading levels.
- Body text: `text-base` (16px) minimum on desktop. Never go below `text-sm` (14px) on mobile for readable content.
- Heading letter-spacing: `tracking-tight` for h1-h2 display text, `tracking-normal` for body.
- Line length: `max-w-prose` (65ch) or `max-w-2xl` for body text paragraphs. Long lines are unreadable.
- Font weights: use at most 3 weights per typeface on a single page (e.g., 400 regular, 500 medium, 700 bold). No weight soup.
- Subtext/captions: `text-sm text-muted-foreground` or equivalent — clearly subordinate to body text.

### Color & Contrast

- All body text must meet WCAG AA contrast ratio: 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text (18px+ bold or 24px+).
- Never use pure black (#000000) on pure white (#FFFFFF). Use softer pairs like #111 on #FAFAFA or #1A1A1A on #F5F5F5.
- Accent color is used sparingly: CTAs, active states, key highlights, and small badges only. Never as a large background area.
- Background hierarchy: page background → card background → nested element background. Each step must be slightly distinct (e.g., #FAFAFA → #FFFFFF → #F5F5F5).
- Never invert the hierarchy (dark card on light page then light nested element).

### Anti-AI-Slop Rules

These patterns are the hallmark of low-quality AI-generated sites. Never use any of them:

- NO generic gradient backgrounds (`bg-gradient-to-r from-blue-500 to-purple-500`). Gradients must be subtle and intentional if used at all.
- NO centered-everything layouts. Body text and lists should be left-aligned (or right-aligned for RTL). Only hero headlines and short CTAs may be centered.
- NO Lorem ipsum or placeholder text anywhere. Every string must be real content.
- NO oversized hero text without clear hierarchy beneath it. If the hero has a large headline, it must be followed by a smaller subheadline and a clear CTA.
- NO shadows on everything. Use box-shadow purposefully: cards, modals, dropdowns, and elevated elements only. Not on text, not on inline elements.
- NO rainbow color schemes. Stick strictly to the defined palette (primary, accent, background, text).
- NO generic stock-photo vibes. Every image must match the brand mood and aesthetic. Use specific Unsplash URLs with relevant keywords.
- NO floating decorative blobs, circles, or abstract shapes unless the design system explicitly calls for them.
- NO excessive border-radius on non-card elements. Inputs, tables, and code blocks stay with subtle rounding (`rounded-md` or `rounded-lg`), not `rounded-3xl`.
- NO using opacity to "soften" poor color choices. Pick the right color instead of slapping `opacity-50` on a wrong one.

### Responsive Design

- Mobile-first: write base styles for 375px, then layer up with `sm:` (640px), `md:` (768px), `lg:` (1024px), `xl:` (1280px).
- Touch targets: minimum 44px × 44px for all interactive elements on mobile (buttons, links, inputs).
- No horizontal scroll on any screen size. Test at 375px minimum.
- Test at these widths: 375px (iPhone SE), 768px (iPad), 1024px (laptop), 1440px (desktop).
- Images: always use `object-cover` with explicit aspect ratios. Never stretch or distort.
- Column stacking on mobile: `grid-cols-1` → `sm:grid-cols-2` → `lg:grid-cols-3`. Never show 3+ columns on mobile.
- Font sizes must scale appropriately — use `clamp()` for hero/display text and fixed sizes with breakpoint overrides for body text.
- Navigation: collapse to hamburger or minimal layout below `md:`. Never show a full horizontal nav on mobile.

### Animation & Interaction

- Every animation must have a purpose: draw attention, indicate state change, or provide feedback. No animation for decoration.
- Duration: 150–300ms for micro-interactions (hover, click, toggle), 500–1000ms for scroll reveals and page transitions.
- Easing: never use `linear` for UI animations. Use `ease-out` for entrances, `ease-in-out` for state changes, custom `cubic-bezier` only when specified.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`: wrap all non-essential animations in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` or check the media query in JS.
- No janky animations: use `transform` and `opacity` (GPU-accelerated) for animated properties. Avoid animating `width`, `height`, `margin`, or `top/left`.
- Hover states: every interactive element must have a visible hover state. Minimum: subtle color shift or `opacity-80`.

### Code Organization

- One component per concern. Do not bundle unrelated UI into a single component.
- Props over hardcoded values. Colors, text, and sizes should be configurable where reuse is expected.
- Semantic HTML: use `<header>`, `<main>`, `<section>`, `<nav>`, `<footer>`, `<article>` appropriately. Not everything is a `<div>`.
- Accessibility: every `<img>` has `alt` text, every `<button>` has an accessible label, every form `<input>` has an associated `<label>`.
- File structure: group by feature or route, not by file type. Components used by a single page live next to that page.
- CSS: use Tailwind utility classes directly. Avoid creating custom CSS classes unless the pattern repeats 3+ times with identical styles.

### Suggested Build Order

**Phase 1 — Project Setup & Auth**
- Initialize project with the chosen framework and package manager.
- Set up the database schema and run migrations.
- Implement authentication (signup, login, password reset, OAuth providers).
- Set up protected routes and middleware.

**Phase 2 — Core Data & API**
- Create database tables/models for all entities defined in the Database Schema section.
- Build CRUD API endpoints for each entity.
- Add input validation, error handling, and rate limiting.
- Set up role-based access control.

**Phase 3 — Frontend Pages & Components**
- Build the shared layout (header, sidebar, footer, navigation).
- Implement each page from the Pages section, starting with the dashboard.
- Build reusable components (forms, tables, modals, cards).
- Wire up API calls and state management.

**Phase 4 — Features & Integrations**
- Implement each feature from the Feature Specification section, starting with core features.
- Connect third-party integrations (payment, email, storage, analytics).
- Add real-time features if specified (WebSockets, subscriptions).

**Phase 5 — Design, Polish & Deploy**
- Apply the design system (colors, fonts, spacing) consistently across all pages.
- Add responsive behavior and test at all breakpoints.
- Implement nice-to-have features.
- Set up CI/CD, environment variables, and deploy.
- Run Lighthouse audit — target 90+ across all categories.
